ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image is a line-angle transition-state drawing; the curved arrows are present but are explicitly ignored. Visually, there is a disconnected cyanide anion labeled NC with a negative charge. The main structure is a large carbocyclic framework containing a bottom alkene with a methyl substituent, a left gem-dimethyl-substituted carbon, a carbon bearing a nitrile substituent, a fused top cyclopropanone fragment with a carbonyl, a methyl substituent on one cyclopropane carbon, a brominated carbon on the right, and a right-side carbon chain closing back to the alkene. Reasoning: Building only the atom-bond graph, the independent cyanide anion is represented as [C-]#N after a dot. Traversing the main ring consistently from the alkene methyl through the alkene and around the ring gives C/C1=C/CC(... )...CC1. The left substituted carbon contributes CC(C)(C), the nitrile-bearing carbon contributes C(C#N), the fused cyclopropanone is encoded as C2C(=O)C2(C), the brominated carbon as C(Br), and the chain closes back to the first ring index. Combining these pieces gives the complete SMILES: C/C1=C/CC(C)(C)C(C#N)C2C(=O)C2(C)C(Br)CC1.[C-]#N.

planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know the required output is a SMILES expression for the transition-state structure and that arrows in the image must be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply standard skeletal-structure conventions and SMILES syntax: unlabeled vertices are carbons with implicit hydrogens; CN attached through carbon is written C#N; free cyanide anion is [C-]#N and separated by a dot; ring closures are marked with digits; carbonyl is C(=O); branches encode methyl, bromo, and nitrile substituents; slash notation can encode the alkene geometry in the selected SMILES traversal.
